about: Settings for M0's simulated groups. These are simulated users, not real ones. Each person independently gets each allergy and halal with the probability below; diet is one of vegan, vegetarian, or none. Probabilities are for US adults, not NC State students.

dairy.source: Gupta RS et al. Prevalence and Severity of Food Allergies Among US Adults. JAMA Netw Open. 2019;2(1):e185630. https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2720064

egg.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above), Table 2, all ages

gluten.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above), Table 2, all ages: wheat allergy

nuts.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above): peanut plus tree nut, added. NC State's "Contains Nuts" covers both. Adding overstates a little, since some people have both.

seafood.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above): shellfish plus fin fish, added. NC State's "Contains Seafood" covers both. Adding overstates a little.

sesame.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above), Table 2, all ages

soy.source: Gupta et al. 2019 (above), Table 2, all ages

pork.source: Pew Research Center, Jewish Americans in 2020 (2021): 2.4% of US adults are Jewish, and 17% of them keep kosher at home; 0.024 x 0.17 = 0.004. Halal (below) covers Muslims separately. https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/2021/05/11/jewish-practices-and-customs/ and https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2021/05/11/10-key-findings-about-jewish-americans/
pork.quote: 17% of U.S. Jews keep kosher at home; 2.4% of U.S. adults are Jewish

halal.source: Pew Research Center, New estimates show U.S. Muslim population continues to grow (2018). Treats every Muslim as keeping halal, which overstates it. https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2018/01/03/new-estimates-show-u-s-muslim-population-continues-to-grow/
halal.quote: Muslims made up about 1.1% of the total U.S. population (2017)

diet.source: Gallup, Snapshot: Few Americans Vegetarian or Vegan (2023). https://news.gallup.com/poll/510038/identify-vegetarian-vegan.aspx
diet.quote: about 4% of Americans identify as vegetarian and 1% as vegan
